LibreOffice documents can contain Basic macro libraries. A library protected by a password is stored in the document in a compiled form, which may be read when the document is loaded. When a value in the compiled form used an older record format, it could be read as a different type from the one the existing value held, which corrupted memory. In fixed versions the existing value is cleared before a value in the older format is read.

LibreOffice Writer can open HTML documents, and an HTML document can bind macros to events of the document as a whole, such as the document being opened or closed. Macros bound to these events were not taken into account by the macro security check, so they could run when the document was opened, whatever the macro security level. In fixed versions these macros follow the macro security settings like any other macro in the document.

LibreOffice documents can contain Basic macro libraries. A library protected by a password is stored in the document in a compiled form, which may be read when the document is loaded. An out-of-bounds write existed when the compiled form was read, because the positions of its strings were not checked against the size of the data they refer to, and a type found by name was not checked to be of the right kind. In fixed versions these positions are checked, a library that fails the check is not loaded, and a type of the wrong kind is ignored.

HtmlSanitizer is a .NET library for cleaning HTML fragments and documents from constructs that can lead to XSS attacks. Prior to 9.0.967 and 9.1.968-beta, HtmlSanitizer CSS style-declaration sanitization can process an attacker-controlled style attribute with quadratic cost because SanitizeStyleDeclaration repeatedly causes the complete declaration to be serialized while removing disallowed CSS properties. One unauthenticated request can occupy a synchronous application worker for seconds, and concurrent requests can saturate all workers and sustain denial of service. This issue is fixed in versions 9.0.967 and 9.1.968-beta.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, and 1.6.1, bws_srv_start() in ports/linux/websocket-srv.c builds the libwebsockets server context with a CA certificate loaded but never sets LWS_SERVER_OPTION_REQUIRE_VALID_OPENSSL_CLIENT_CERT, so the hub accepts TLS connections from clients presenting no certificate at all. Any network-reachable host can join the BACnet/SC mesh without credentials. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, 1.6.1, and 1.7.0.
IBM i 7.6, 7.5, 7.4, and 7.3 could allow an authenticated user to indirectly disable system auditing, which they otherwise don't have authority to disable.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation Mediawiki - UserPageViewTracker Extension allows SQL Injection.

This issue affects Mediawiki - UserPageViewTracker Extension: from * before 1.46.1, 1.45.5, 1.43.10.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260416.0, public TAXII 2.1 collections configured with taxii_public set to true are served under the high-privilege SYSTEM_USER context rather than a restricted public-sharing user context. Unauthenticated requests can therefore bypass object markings, organization segregation, and authorized_members restrictions and retrieve restricted threat-intelligence objects that match the collection filters; a broad or absent filter can expose most of the database. Version 7.260416.0 remediates this issue for new configurations, but public-sharing configurations created before that version are not covered and are tracked separately in GHSA-25r9-q6rp-j7jw.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 14.0 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to create issues with locked discussions despite lacking the required permissions due to improper authorization checks.
IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty 17.0.0.3 through 26.0.0.10 could allow an authenticated user with the Reader role to obtain sensitive information.

Instatic is an open source visual content management system for building static websites. Prior to 0.0.14, isSafeUrl() and safeUrl() in src/core/html-sanitize/index.ts remove tabs, newlines, carriage returns, and characters handled by String.prototype.trim(), but leave other leading C0 control characters that browsers discard before parsing a URL scheme. A low-privileged editor can place a dangerous URL behind one of those controls in a URL property or custom HTML attribute, allowing src/core/publisher/escapeProps.ts and the shared URL sanitizer to emit it into rendered content. When an Owner or Admin activates the element in the same-origin admin editor canvas, script executes with the victim's application authority and can drive admin APIs to read protected data, create an owner account, or install a plugin. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.14.

Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320, a registered user can supply path traversal sequences in the hash field accepted by POST /api/attachments/signature when the default local storage provider is in use. In apps/nestjs-backend/src/features/attachments/plugins/local.ts, LocalStorage.presigned uses the client-controlled hash as the storage filename, and LocalStorage.save resolves that path and copies the uploaded request body without calling assertPathWithinStorage on the write path. The read path uses the jail, but the write path does not, allowing the resolved destination to escape the configured storage directory. Because the backend container runs as uid 0, the attacker can write or overwrite arbitrary root-owned files, which can corrupt the instance or lead to root code execution. Object-storage deployments that do not use LocalStorage.save are not affected by this sink. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260715.0, a ProfileQuery response can expose the user's TOTP MFA secret after activation. A person who can access the profile response can recover the secret, enroll a duplicate authenticator, and generate valid one-time codes, undermining the account's second-factor protection. This issue is fixed in version 7.260715.0.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. In 7.260722.0 and earlier, a user with the SETTINGS_SETCUSTOMIZATION capability can configure a webhook notifier with an arbitrary destination URL and invoke notifierTest to make the OpenCTI server send the request immediately. The request can target internal services or cloud metadata endpoints that are reachable from the server, enabling server-side request forgery without waiting for a notifier event. No fixed release is verified by the available evidence; later releases remain unclassified.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 13.4 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to view iteration details from private groups they did not have access to due to missing authorization checks.

Chevereto before 4.5.8 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to cause the server to issue arbitrary requests by supplying a malicious URL to the uploadToWebsite function, which fetches the raw source via fetch_url before the Upload::checkValidUrl SSRF guard can be invoked. Attackers can target loopback addresses, RFC1918 internal services, cloud instance metadata endpoints, and file/gopher/dict schemes through the /json upload action to disclose internal responses or credentials when the fetched content is stored and served back as a public image URL.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260428.0, the token GraphQL mutation used for primary login has no endpoint-specific rate limit, while the global Express limiter defaults to permitting 10,000 requests in a one-second window. An unauthenticated remote attacker can make password guesses at network speed against a chosen user account and, if a credential is recovered, access the account's threat-intelligence data and permitted operations. This issue is fixed in version 7.260428.0.

A maliciously crafted DWG file, when parsed by Autodesk AutoCAD, can trigger an Integer Overflow vulnerability in RLE bitmap decompression, resulting in an undersized heap allocation and subsequent heap buffer overflow. A malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to cause a crash or potentially execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 17.7 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read GitLab Duo seat assignments and usage data from other groups due to improper authorization checks.

LibreOffice can embed audio and video in documents. Where it plays media with GStreamer, as on Linux, the media is opened when the document is loaded, and a preview image of a video is shown in the document and in its exports, such as PDF. A crafted media file could make GStreamer read a local file and draw its text into the preview image, so that the content of the file ended up in an exported document. This is a different route to the problem fixed for CVE-2026-63269. In fixed versions GStreamer opens only media in a short list of common, self-contained container formats.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.30.0, flash late-interaction scoring at the /score and /rerank endpoints derives each worker's query_key value from the caller-controlled X-Request-Id header. A concurrent request that reuses a victim's identifier can overwrite the cached query embedding so the victim's documents are scored against the attacker's query, and shared use counters can also cause a late-interaction cache-miss error. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.

A flaw was found in CRI-O. When the optional Linux LinkLogs feature is enabled, the host pod log directory is bind-mounted into a pod emptyDir and is intended to be read-only, but Linux ignores MS_RDONLY on the initial bind and the CRI mount stays writable. A non-privileged UID 0 container can place a symlink at a future kubelet log path so that privileged conmon later appends attacker-controlled log data to an existing host file. This is an append-only host integrity issue, not universal remote code execution; LinkLogs is not enabled by default.

An out-of-bounds read in SCRAM authentication response parsing in the MongoDB C Driver can read one byte beyond a fixed-size buffer when processing a malformed server-final message. A server or network intermediary able to provide this message before server-signature verification can cause the application using the driver to terminate. The extra byte is not returned through the protocol.

An integer underflow in the KMS endpoint-parsing logic of MongoDB libmongocrypt can cause an allocation failure that terminates the application process. This can occur when an authenticated user modifies a key document in the key vault collection, or when an application accepts a KMS endpoint containing a colon after its path or query during key creation. The issue does not access memory outside its allocated bounds.

The MongoDB C++ Driver discards content after an embedded NUL byte in certain field and collection names accepted by the collection API. This can cause the driver and the calling application to interpret the same name differently. An authenticated actor who can influence a name passed by an affected application can cause the application to read distinct values from an unintended field or rename an unintended collection. These operations use the application's existing database credentials.

An off-by-one error in the BSON bulk document writer in the MongoDB C Driver can write one zero byte immediately past a heap allocation when a document ends at a specific buffer boundary. An actor who can influence the size of documents serialized by an embedding application can corrupt adjacent process memory or terminate the process. Reaching this issue requires the application to use the BSON bulk-writer API and produce a precise cumulative document size.

libvisio is a library that reads drawings in the VSD and VSDX formats. LibreOffice and other applications use it to import such drawings. An out-of-bounds write existed when a crafted VSDX file contained a malformed path from one part of the drawing to another. In fixed versions a malformed path is handled without writing outside its data.

U.S. Geological Survey Area Species Management Research Program (ARMI) accepts any uploaded file and stores the file under '/uploads/{upload-file}'. A remote, authenticated attacker could upload a crafted PHP file that executes and returns command output from the server when accessed. Fixed on 2026-07-20.

Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails,
OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones and any new
ones, but leaves them in the stack.

Impact summary: An application that passes an existing stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a failed read may
use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash or, in
principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make the read fail,
but only applications that pass an existing stack are affected, and
OpenSSL itself does not do this.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads certificates, CRLs and
private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of X509_INFO
structures. If the application passes a stack that is not NULL, the
function adds the new entries to it and must leave the entries that are
already there unchanged.

If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the stack. This
includes the entries that were there before the call, and the entries
added by the call. It does not remove these entries from the stack, so
the stack keeps pointers to freed memory. The failure can happen at any
point, even before any entry was added. A PEM item with invalid content
is enough.  This also happens if the stack was empty: entries added
before the failure are freed but stay in the stack.

An application that then reads or frees the stack will use memory that
was already freed. This can crash the application or, in principle,
corrupt memory.

Only applications that pass a stack that is not NULL are affected.
OpenSSL itself never does this. Its own callers, including the code that
TLS uses to load CA certificates, always pass NULL. When the stack is
NULL, the function frees only the entries that it created itself, which
is safe. We expect that very few applications pass an existing stack. An
attacker can make the read fail with malformed PEM data, but cannot make
an application pass an existing stack.

The same problem affects PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(), PEM_X509_INFO_read()
and PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex(), which use the same code. OpenSSL 1.1.1 and
1.0.2 have only the first two of these functions.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a remote malicious QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.

The Bizuno Accounting – ERP/Accounting/CRM (for WordPress) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Password Reset Token Disclosure in all versions up to, and including, 7.4.5 via the `bizUser` parameter of the `validateReset()` function on the `portal/api/lostPW` endpoint. This is due to `portalCtl::goAPI()` failing to call `loadBusinessCache()` before invoking the handler, which causes `isMailConfigured()` to read an empty business cache and return false regardless of the site's actual mail configuration, causing the fully-qualified reset URL — containing the victim's live reset UUID and numeric user ID — to be embedded directly in the HTML response rather than delivered by email. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to obtain a valid password-reset token for any Bizuno account, including administrators, directly from the HTTP response and submit it to the `portal/api/lostVal` endpoint to rewrite the victim's password and achieve full account takeover. The administrator email address required to initiate the reset is frequently exposed by the plugin's own login error messages and the public `/bizuno/` portal page, making exploitation trivial against most installations.

tiny-secp256k1 is a tiny secp256k1 native/JS wrapper. From 2.1.0 until 2.2.5 for tiny-secp256k1 and from 2.2.2 until 2.2.5 for @bitcoin-js/tiny-secp256k1-asmjs, the three-argument xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck path ignores the backend failure return from xOnlyPointAddTweak when a tweak produces the point at infinity. The shared X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_INPUT buffer then still contains the original point, so a caller-controlled resultToCheck equal to that point can make the stale-buffer comparison return true even though no tweaked key exists. Protocols that rely on this helper to validate caller-controlled internal keys, tweaks, and comparison values can accept an invalid derived key. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.5.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to second-order SQL Injection via the user profile description field in all Free versions up to, and including, 1.26.15 and all Premium versions up to, and including, 2.26.15. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to store a malicious payload that is written into a database backup and executed as SQL when an administrator later restores that backup. Successful exploitation can modify sensitive WordPress data and, on sites where plugin installation is available, lead to remote code execution through the installation and activation of an attacker-controlled plugin.

PLANET GS-5220-8P2T2S (hardware version 3.0) firmware versions before 3.2412b261008 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to corrupt stack memory by submitting an oversized webstax_auth HTTP Cookie value that is copied into a fixed-size stack buffer without length validation. Attackers can send a crafted unauthenticated HTTP request with an oversized cookie to overwrite the saved return address and corrupt stack memory, leading to memory corruption and potential denial of service on the device.

OmniFaces is a utility library for Faces. From 5.2 until 5.4.3, applications using <o:sse> or @Push(type=SSE) with session scope, view scope, or a user attribute can expose pushed messages because org.omnifaces.cdi.push.SseEndpoint#doGet accepts a channel identifier registered by SseChannelManager and PushSessionManager without verifying that the caller's HTTP session owns it. An attacker who obtains the victim's channel identifier from a logged URL, report, Referer header, or shared link can connect from a foreign or absent session and receive messages intended for the victim. Application-scoped channels are intentionally unbound, and this issue permits message receipt but not message injection. This issue is fixed in version 5.4.3.

IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway 1.0.0 through 1.0.11 could allow an authenticated caller to bypass upstream credential-level authorization policies due to an insufficiently specific cache key in the RFC 8693 token exchange cache, enabling reuse of cached upstream bearer tokens across different credentials belonging to the same user.

An incorrect authorization vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated user whose numeric user ID matched an enterprise's numeric ID to manage that enterprise's GitHub Apps and generate private keys without enterprise membership. GitHub App ownership checks compared numeric IDs without checking the owner's account type. Exploitation required control of a session for the colliding user account and an enterprise-owned GitHub App. A generated private key could be used to authenticate as the App and access repositories where it was installed, within its granted permissions. On standard fresh installations, the documented collision involved the non-loginable built-in ghost account; the reported GHES reproduction used site administrator impersonation. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

The Libreswan pluto daemon dereferences a NULL pointer when a CERT payload is received with an empty PKCS#7 payload, causing the daemon to crash and restart. The NSS function SEC_PKCS7GetCertificateList() was used to check whether the content was empty, but this check did not trigger if the non-empty content of the PKCS#7 wrapped payload was an empty list. Continued triggering of this vulnerability can lead to a denial of service. Remote code execution is not possible. Authentication is not required to trigger this vulnerability.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.

Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport. A self-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) identified the user only by numeric user ID, and a new user takes the lowest free ID. After an administrator deleted a user, that user's unexpired token, or a token refreshed from it while the ID was free, authenticated as the next account created with that ID and had that account's permissions. Only deployments with HTTP enabled are affected.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: through 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 11.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read Git LFS objects from projects restricted by External Authorization due to missing authorization checks.

The SimpleSAMLphp SAML2 library is a PHP library for SAML2 related functionality. From 6.2.2 until 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2, HTTPArtifact::receive() in src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php verifies a signed outer ArtifactResponse but returns an unsigned embedded SAML Response before calling verifyMessageSignature(). The signed path verifies with the artifact issuer's metadata keys without requiring the embedded Response issuer to match that artifact issuer. In a multi-IdP federation, an attacker controlling one trusted IdP can therefore return a validly signed outer ArtifactResponse containing an unsigned Response that claims a different IdP, bypassing the binding's embedded-message authentication. End-to-end impersonation requires a service provider using HTTP-Artifact and a downstream consumer that relies on the binding to authenticate the embedded Response rather than independently requiring a signature. This issue is fixed in versions 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2.

libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 5.1.22, the @libp2p/crypto code reached by the default Identify service accepts a remote peer’s crafted publicKey before peer-id or signature verification and passes it through publicKeyFromProtobuf to the ASN.1 DER decoder. readLength in packages/crypto/src/keys/rsa/der.ts accepts long-form element lengths larger than the remaining buffer, causing readInteger and related readers to loop synchronously over an attacker-claimed length from a very small key blob. Because decoding occurs in one event-loop tick before the remotePeer equality check in packages/protocol-identify/src/identify.ts, the Identify timeout cannot interrupt it, allowing repeated unauthenticated connections to stall all timers and peers and transiently exhaust memory. This issue is fixed in version 5.1.22.

The Trust Payments Gateway for WooCommerce (JavaScript Library) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.8. The vulnerability exists because the `new_customer_account()` function stores the raw return value of `wp_create_user()` — including a `WP_Error` object returned on username collision — into the order's `tp_userid` post meta before the `is_wp_error()` guard is evaluated; the `add_customer_details_to_thankyou_page()` callback subsequently reads that meta and casts it with `(int)`, causing PHP to coerce any object to integer `1`, after which `wp_set_current_user(1)` and `wp_set_auth_cookie(1)` are called unconditionally. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as WordPress user ID 1 — the bootstrap site administrator or, on multisite, a network super-admin — by supplying the `new_username` parameter matching any existing login during checkout and visiting the resulting thank-you page. Exploitation requires the Trust Payments gateway to be active and the attacker to complete a paid order on their own account; the ID 1 administrator username is additionally enumerable via standard WordPress user enumeration techniques.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 17.1.7 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed sensitive credential values submitted in GraphQL requests to be written to logs in plaintext due to incomplete filtering of sensitive data.

Netgate pfSense CE 2.7.0 through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with QinQ edit privilege to run commands by storing an unvalidated parent interface name. Attackers can save a crafted 'if' value, then edit the QinQ entry so it is interpolated into ifconfig shell commands, executing commands as root.

Netgate pfSense CE through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute commands as root by supplying a crafted wireless parent interface name. Attackers with limited Wireless Edit or Interface Assignments privileges can submit values like ath0;<cmd> via interfaces_wireless_edit.php or interfaces_assign.php, which interface_wireless_clone() interpolates unescaped into an ifconfig shell command.

Netgate pfSense CE through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with gateway edit privileges to execute commands as root by injecting shell metacharacters into an IPv6 link-local zone index. Attackers can set a gateway Monitor IP whose unvalidated zone carries a payload, which start_dpinger() passes unescaped to the dpinger shell command when monitoring is applied.

Netgate pfSense CE through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with Virtual IP edit privileges to execute commands as root by storing an unvalidated CARP VHID. Attackers can supply a VHID containing shell metacharacters that executes via interface_ipalias_configure() ifconfig calls or get_carp_interface_status() when CARP status is rendered.

Netgate pfSense CE 2.7.0 through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with Traffic Shaper Limiters privileges to execute root commands by tampering with the limiter number field. Attackers can submit a malicious hidden 'number' value when editing a limiter, then delete it so delete_queue() passes the unquoted value to dnctl via /bin/sh as root.

Netgate pfSense CE through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains a newline injection vulnerability in services_pppoe_edit.php that allows privileged users to inject mpd.secret entries via unvalidated username POST fields. Attackers with the PPPoE Server Edit privilege can add a line whose secret begins with '!', making mpd5 run commands as root when a PPPoE client authenticates.

pfSense CE through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains a crontab injection vulnerability in interfaces_ppps_edit.php that allows authenticated users to execute commands as root by injecting newlines into the ptpid or reset hour/minute fields. Attackers holding the 'WebCfg - Interfaces: PPPs: Edit' privilege can submit crafted POST values that configure_cron() writes unescaped into /etc/crontab, running arbitrary root commands on schedule.

Netgate pfSense CE through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains a php.ini injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with General Setup privileges to inject directives by submitting an unvalidated timezone value. Attackers can embed a quote and newline to add auto_prepend_file pointing at /var/db/zoneinfo, executing PHP as root after php.ini is regenerated at boot or php-fpm restart.

Netgate pfSense CE 2.7.0 through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains a configuration injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with IPsec Mobile privileges to execute commands as root via the login_banner field. Attackers can submit a single-line banner containing '}' to escape the unquoted strongswan.conf attr value and define charon.start-scripts entries that charon executes as root on restart.

pfSense CE through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the OpenVPN openvpn.connect_async.sh script that allows authenticated VPN users to execute commands as root via crafted usernames. Attackers authenticated through RADIUS or LDAP can use usernames containing single quotes and shell metacharacters to break out of the eval'd pfctl anchor name on connect or disconnect.

Netgate pfSense CE 2.5.0 through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in openvpn.learn-address.sh that allows authenticated VPN clients to execute commands as the unbound user. Attackers can embed shell metacharacters in the certificate common name or username, which is interpolated unquoted into su -c strings, when DNS Resolver client registration is enabled.

pfSense CE 2.4.5 through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated WebGUI users with Advanced Admin Access privilege to execute commands as root via Login Protection settings. Attackers can submit sshguard threshold, block time, or detection time values containing newlines or $(...) that are written unvalidated to sshguard.conf and sourced as root on restart.

Netgate pfSense CE through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains a CRLF injection vulnerability in services_unbound_acls.php that allows authenticated users with the DNS Resolver: Access Lists privilege to inject Unbound configuration directives. Attackers can embed CR/LF characters in the aclname or aclaction fields written to access_lists.conf to add local-data, local-zone, or forward-zone directives and control DNS answers served to LAN clients.

Netgate pfSense CE from 2.7.1 through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains a CRLF injection vulnerability in services_unbound_advanced.php that allows authenticated users with DNS Resolver: Advanced privilege to inject Unbound directives. Attackers can embed CR/LF characters in the unvalidated sock_queue_timeout parameter, which is written raw into unbound.conf, to override local records and forwarding for all clients.

Netgate pfSense CE through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains a local file read vulnerability that allows users with the Dynamic DNS client privilege to read files as root by setting a file:// custom Update URL in services_dyndns_edit.php. Attackers can set a non-matching Result Match string so _checkStatus() logs file contents such as /conf/config.xml or /etc/master.passwd to the system log.

Netgate pfSense CE 2.3.0 through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with Firewall: Rules or NAT: Port Forward privileges to inject scripts via the separator color field. Attackers can submit a crafted separator[] color value that display_separator() renders unencoded into class attributes, executing in administrators' browsers to perform WebGUI actions with their privileges.

Netgate pfSense CE 2.7.1 through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in firewall_rules.php that allows remote attackers to inject script via the unencoded if parameter. When the non-default Require Firewall Interface option is enabled, attackers can lure users with firewall rules privileges into opening a crafted GET link to execute script in the WebGUI with their privileges.

The SchemaEngine AI – AI Schema Markup, Reviews & Rich Snippets for SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'content/excerpt (REST wp/v2/posts) → stored in post_content/post_excerpt' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Contributor's entity-encoded payload survives save-time wp_kses filtering verbatim and is only decoded into raw script tags at render time via html_entity_decode(), meaning the injected script executes for every visitor — including authenticated Administrators — once an Editor publishes the post through the standard Contributor workflow.
Dell PowerStore contains an authorization bypass vulnerability. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to act under another user's session, potentially leading to denial of service.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.0 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to hide changes from reviewers in merge request diffs due to improper handling of file names.

An authorization bypass through user-controlled key vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed authenticated users to read review-thread data from private repositories they could not access. An attacker required an authenticated account, a readable repository and pull request to use as the request context, and target review-thread identifiers. The thread-preview endpoint resolved supplied identifiers without restricting them to the authorized pull request, exposing private file paths and, when positioning and diff data were available, source-code excerpts, commit identifiers, and line metadata without victim interaction. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases in the 3.21, 3.22 series and was fixed in versions 3.21.10, 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

The Event Tickets with Ticket Scanner plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'code' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload persists through WooCommerce session data into order-item metadata and executes when rendered in the ticket scanner interface.

A command injection vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated site administrator to execute arbitrary commands as the host git user on peer Git server nodes outside the pre-receive hook sandbox by supplying a crafted pre-receive environment download URL. Exploitation required a clustered deployment using custom pre-receive hook environments and at least one peer Git server node. This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.22.5, 3.21.10, 3.20.12, and 3.19.16. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a mail proxy, undisclosed traffic can cause a use-after-free in an nginx worker process. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
A remote unauthenticated attacker may crash an nginx worker process or corrupt its memory, disrupting service. Remote code execution is a potential impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. From 21.14.8 until 21.14.10, the app-data seeder can leave an environment linked to temporary package files that virtualenv deletes when creation finishes. The environment-variable and configuration-file forms of symlink_app_data can enable this state even though the command-line flag is disabled for temporary app-data. The resulting environment depends on a cache pathname that its owner no longer controls. This issue is fixed in version 21.14.10.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.14.9, download_wheel() writes package-index downloads directly into the reusable wheel/house cache before selecting a verification target from pip's textual Saved output. With default-index digest comparison enabled, a controlled package index can inject a misleading Saved line through a discarded link's data-requires-python attribute; this forged-line variant also requires knowledge of an absolute path to the genuine bundled wheel. The wrong path can then be hashed, while a digest mismatch leaves the rejected archive in the cache for later selection without verification. A separate rejected-cache-file variant requires control over downloaded data or archive selection but not the forged-line prerequisites. Explicit custom-index exceptions are outside the promised PyPI comparison, and the issue does not independently bypass TLS or establish control of default PyPI. This issue is fixed in version 21.14.9.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.14.9, the stdlib venv creator reads generated pyvenv.cfg with str.splitlines() and merges parsed keys over virtualenv's selected configuration. An untrusted caller who influences the destination pathname can include a line-boundary character such as U+2028 to inject keys including home and include-system-site-packages, causing path data to change configuration structure before final output. Setting include-system-site-packages to true weakens environment isolation, while an altered home can change which standard-library files the interpreter loads if the attacker also controls that location. The builtin creator does not use this readback path. This issue is fixed in version 21.14.9.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.14.9, the builtin creator calls ensure_dir() for executable, library, and package directories, and ensure_dir() accepts an existing symlink to a directory because exists() follows it. Interpreter creation, seed installation, and activation generation then write through the linked parent outside the requested destination when another local account prepared the tree and the invoking user can access the target. The --clear option removes the planted tree first, while ordinary creation reaches it; arbitrary attacker-selected output bytes are not established. This issue is fixed in version 21.14.9.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.14.9, PipInvoke.get_pip_install_cmd() handles --seeder pip --download by calling get_wheel(download=False) and then allowing pip to consult the configured index, bypassing virtualenv's download_wheel() and verify_wheel_digest() path. When virtualenv's default-index PyPI digest comparison remains enabled, an index candidate matching the bundled package and version can therefore be selected without comparison to PyPI SHA-256 metadata. Explicit custom-index settings already opt out of that comparison and remain outside this verification-bypass claim; the demonstrated configuration used a non-PyPI index while leaving the index environment variables unset so the comparison policy remained active. This condition does not independently defeat TLS or establish control of the index response. This issue is fixed in version 21.14.9.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.14.9, POSIX xonsh activation quote() uses repr() to write printable non-ASCII prompt or destination data into UTF-8 activate.xsh, while xonsh can read that script using $XONSH_ENCODING. Under a legacy multibyte codec such as GBK or Big5, a UTF-8 trail byte can consume the backslash before an adjacent quote, allowing the literal to close and attacker-influenced statements to execute when the user sources the generated script. This issue is fixed in version 21.14.9.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.14.9, PipInstall._uninstall_previous_version() accepts existing seed-package metadata and _uninstall_dist() joins entries from top_level.txt and RECORD to site-packages without checking containment. When a reused destination contains distribution metadata influenced by another account, relative traversal, absolute entries, or linked parents can cause app-data reseeding to delete files outside the environment or the environment root with the invoking user's permissions, provided that user has deletion rights over the named paths. The deletion occurs during environment creation before any later use of the environment. Fresh environments without existing package metadata and creation with --clear do not enter this cleanup path. This issue is fixed in version 21.14.9.

ESP-IDF is the Espressif Internet of Things (IoT) Development Framework. Prior to 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.5.6, and 6.0.3, the Bluedroid BLE Mesh GATT server read handler bt_mesh_bta_gatts_cb in esp_ble_mesh stores a signed attribute-read callback length in an unsigned 16-bit variable. A negative ATT error code is therefore interpreted as a very large successful length and used for a memory copy from a small stack buffer into the GATT response structure. A remote attacker within Bluetooth LE range who can connect to an exposed PB-GATT provisioning or Mesh Proxy service can trigger a failed attribute read with a crafted request. On devices where the affected attributes are accessible without pairing, exploitation requires neither pairing nor user interaction; access requirements depend on device configuration. The resulting out-of-bounds read and stack-based buffer overflow corrupts the Bluetooth host task stack, causing a crash and device restart and potentially further memory corruption. The issue affects devices built with CONFIG_BT_BLUEDROID_ENABLED=y and BLE Mesh GATT enabled; the NimBLE host path is not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.5.6, and 6.0.3.

Eclipse Kura downloads deployment packages (DPs) from a remote URL without any limit on the size of the data it receives. A malicious or compromised HTTP(S) server, or an attacker able to tamper with a plain-HTTP download, can stream an arbitrarily large (or endless) response. Kura writes the response to local storage until the filesystem is full. On gateways the temporary directory is often a RAM-backed tmpfs, so this can also exhaust memory. The result is denial of service of the device: failed configuration persistence, failed logging and possible crashes of the framework or other services.



The same missing size limit is present in the REST upload endpoint `POST /deploy/v2/_upload`, which copies the request body to the temporary directory with no limit.



Workarounds: only install DPs from trusted HTTPS sources, restrict who can install packages (Web UI `kura.packages.admin` permission, REST `kura.permission.rest.deploy`, cloud DEPLOY-V2 access).

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260722.0, the GraphQL endpoint accepts query operations over HTTP GET because CSRF prevention is disabled (csrfPrevention: false), placing the complete GraphQL query and its arguments in the request URL. Server and reverse-proxy logs, browser history, and shared caches can retain sensitive filters, marking-restricted identifiers, and investigation search arguments, allowing a person with access to those records to recover legitimate users' query contents. GraphQL mutations are not accepted over GET, and the issue does not permit code execution. This issue is fixed in version 7.260722.0.
