GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.8 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read NuGet package metadata that should not have been accessible due to missing authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to enable Amazon Q automatic code reviews on a project despite an administrator lock due to improper enforcement of instance-level settings.

Incorrect quota accounting in Progress Software WS_FTP Server releases prior to 2025.0.5 on Windows could allow an authenticated user with upload and delete permissions to exceed storage quotas, potentially causing denial of service.

Improper access control in Progress WS_FTP Server versions prior to 2025.0.5 could allow an authenticated user with certain folder-management permissions to bypass access restrictions and access or modify files belonging to other users.

Insufficient protection of communications in Progress WS_FTP Server versions prior to 2025.0.5 could allow a network attacker to intercept sensitive information or modify requests when unencrypted connections are used.
Insufficient resource limits in Progress Software WS_FTP Server releases prior to 2025.0.5 on Windows could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause denial of service.
Progress Software WS_FTP Server versions prior to 2025.0.5 on Windows may write sensitive user credential and session data to a temporary file during file transfer operations.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 17.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with a valid agent token to cause a denial of service in the GitLab agent server (KAS) due to improper input validation.
IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty 17.0.0.3 through 26.0.0.10 is affected by a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the Admin Center deploy validation endpoint.

Doorkeeper is an OAuth 2 provider for Ruby on Rails / Grape. Prior to 5.9.1, Doorkeeper's OAuth token revocation flow does not correctly authorize revocation requests when public, non-confidential clients are used, allowing tokens to be revoked without correct authorization. This issue is fixed in version 5.9.1.

In specific versions of Octopus Tentacle, Tentacle fails to unset registration credentials as environment variables, resulting in deployment scripts potentially having the ability to read those credentials.

Deserialization of untrusted data in the report-processing code of Puppet, as used by Puppet Server, in the affected releases, allows a client that holds any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as its service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type via PUT request. Where the certificate authority autosigns requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain such a certificate.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 19.1 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to view unredacted secret values from secret detection findings they had access to through GitLab Duo Agent Platform due to improper authorization checks.
IBM App Connect Operator and IBM App Connect Enterprise Certified Containers Operands is vulnerable to Log Forging on a request to create a resource.

The Kirki – Freeform Page Builder, Website Builder & Customizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (title attribute of <abbr>)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.4.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to run the Kirki Convert (migration) workflow on a page containing the attacker's approved comment, as the browser-side DOM parser decodes the kses-allowed abbr title attribute value into a raw XSS payload that is then persisted without sanitization and later rendered unescaped. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The rus to lat advanced plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to blind SQL Injection via the 'name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

The Multi Step for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.1 via the '_cf7mls_db_form_data_id' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to permanently delete arbitrary stored Contact Form 7 submissions from the database. Exploitation requires the companion CF7 Database plugin to be active and the per-form "Save every step, not just the final submission" option to be enabled.

The Libreswan IKEv2 state machine did not verify that an IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange was required to satisfy the addke= PostQuantum algorithm component of the exchange. A connecting client could (maliciously or by implementation error) skip the IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange and start an IKE_AUTH exchange prematurely. The result is as if the addke= option had not been specified, and such connections are only protected by the classic key exchange algorithm (such as P-256 or Curve25519), allowing "store now, decrypt later" attacks once a quantum computer becomes available. Only connections with the addke= keyword in the ike= and/or esp= configuration option are affected. PostQuantum Hybrid Key Exchange support was added in version 5.4.

The FS Poster - WordPress Social media Auto Poster & Scheduler [Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Pinterest] plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to missing authorization to Unauthorized Social App Data Modification in all versions up to, and including, 8.0.1 This is due to missing authentication, nonce, and capability checks in the `standardFSApp()` function, which is registered on the `wp` action hook and executes on every frontend page load without any login or permission verification. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to insert arbitrary social network app records into the database, or overwrite the OAuth `client_id` and `client_secret` of existing social network connections, by supplying attacker-controlled values via the `fsp_app_redirect` and `app` GET parameters. An attacker can target a specific existing social app record for credential overwrite by supplying matching `social_network` and `slug` values, requiring no knowledge of internal record IDs, which disrupts scheduled social media posts and forces administrators to re-authenticate their connected accounts.

A vulnerability was determined in EyouCMS up to 1.8.6. This impacts the function remote_file_to_local of the file application/function.php. Executing a manipulation can lead to server-side request forgery. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. Upgrading to version 1.8.7 will fix this issue. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

Dell PowerScale InsightIQ, versions 6.3.0 through 6.4.0, contains a Weak Password Requirements vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information disclosure and Unauthorized access.

Dell PowerScale InsightIQ, versions 6.3.0 through 6.4.0, containsan Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information disclosure.
Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains an out-of-bounds memory vulnerability in the NAS NFS service that an unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit to cause a denial of service.
Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability that could allow an attacker with internal network access to execute arbitrary commands as root on the NAS node.

The Check & Log Email – Easy Email Testing & Mail logging plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires an administrator to approve the comment carrying the shortcode payload, and the target page must render the core Latest Comments block, which passes comment author names through do_shortcode via the_content.

The Custom Twitter Feeds – A Tweets Widget or X Feed Widget plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'atts (JSON object, specifically the inner `feed` key)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload is first stored in the wp_ctf_feed_caches database table and later written into the ctf_cron_report WordPress option by the scheduled ctf_feed_update cron job, meaning execution is deferred until the cron runs and an administrator subsequently loads the Support page.

The Jeg Kit for Elementor – Powerful Addons for Elementor, Widgets & Templates for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful execution requires a published page containing both a Post Author widget in user_bio mode (rendering the attacker's biography) and any legitimate jkit_client_logo widget, so that client-logo.js is enqueued and the loadCarousel handler fires against the forged widget markup from the bio field.

A site administrator could modify files on the appliance host with root privileges and disclose private repository data due to improper path validation in GitHub Enterprise Server. Exploitation required a crafted pre-receive hook environment. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server versions prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

An SSH certificate authentication bypass vulnerability in GitHub Enterprise Server allowed an authenticated organization member to read and modify another user's private repositories within the trusted certificate authority's scope. Exploitation required an instance using built-in authentication and a valid certificate issued to the attacker by a trusted SSH certificate authority. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.
Tanium addressed an improper access controls vulnerability in Enforce.
Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

The Multi Step for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'multipart field name (array key)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the target CF7 form to have the 'Save every step' option enabled and the Database for Contact Form 7 companion plugin to be active with its 'Expandable' table option enabled, both of which are disabled by default.

The Advanced Country Blocker plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected script is stored via the advcb_live_activity transient on the init hook and executed when an administrator views the Live Monitor page, as the stored URI is unsafely concatenated into a double-quoted HTML title attribute and inserted into the DOM via jQuery .html().

The The GDPR Framework By Data443 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.2. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to delete all postmeta rows for every Easy Digital Downloads payment order on the site, destroying order metadata belonging to all customers. Exploitation requires that Easy Digital Downloads 2.x is active and the GDPR Framework's EDD compatibility option is enabled with a delete or delete_and_notify action configured.

Description:

When an iRule that processes client traffic using the GENERICMESSAGE::route command is configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE). 





Impact:



Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.







Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Typecho before 1.3.1-rc contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the XML-RPC pingback.ping method where checkSafeHost() validates a hostname's resolved IP once but the subsequent outbound request performs an independent DNS resolution, creating a TOCTOU window exploitable via DNS rebinding. An unauthenticated attacker can configure a domain to return a benign IP at validation time and an internal address (loopback, RFC1918, or cloud metadata IP) at request time, causing the server to issue blind SSRF requests to arbitrary internal hosts and ports.

A Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information (CWE-319) vulnerability exists in the Android application "Imperial Palaces Guide" provided by The Imperial Household Agency. A man-in-the-middle attacker may be able to tamper with data transmitted between the application and the server, resulting in the display of modified content to users.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 12.4 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read private CI/CD job artifacts belonging to other projects through GitLab Pages due to improper validation of file paths.

The JobBoardWP – Job Board Listings and Submissions plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'job_description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The plugin's default public submission workflow auto-provisions a jb_employer account for any visitor, meaning the effective entry point is unauthenticated — the custom role requirement imposes no real barrier on a stock install.

Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. If Apache Iggy 0.9.0 started without IGGY_ROOT_USERNAME and IGGY_ROOT_PASSWORD, it generated a root password and wrote it to the server log file, which is enabled by default. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) let a user with only the read_servers permission download the server log files. That user could read the generated root password and log in as root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Version 0.10.0 never generates a root password, and the snapshot requires the manage_servers permission. If a 0.9.0 server generated its root password, change that password.

The CODESYS Automation Server Connector uses server-supplied file names without sufficient path traversal checks. An unauthenticated remote attacker controlling a malicious Automation Server and tricking a user to trust it, or performing a man-in-the-middle attack on a trusted communication channel, can exploit this vulnerability to write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary locations on the engineering workstation and subsequently achieve arbitrary code execution with user privileges.

The DataPress (Dataverse Integration) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 2.97 via the 'src' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. Exploitation requires WP_DEBUG to be defined as true on the target site — not the default on production, but commonly enabled on staging, development, and misconfigured production environments.

Winmate HotTab Exposed Dangerous Function Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of Winmate devices. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the HotTab driver. The issue results from an exposed dangerous function. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of the kernel. Was ZDI-CAN-29948.

Farmasimplex retrieves a CIP News file over HTTP and executes embedded SQL statements against the local FarmaCIP database with administrative privileges. An attacker able to tamper with network communications or compromise vendor infrastructure can inject arbitrary SQL commands, leading to unauthorized access to, modification or deletion of database contents and potentially operating system command execution.

When using the listen directive with the ssl parameter in the http block with TLSv1.3 enabled, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS connection to cause an infinite loop in the NGINX worker process while reading the HTTP request body. As a result, the worker process stops accepting new connections and processing existing connections. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Impact: This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) of NGINX. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 17.11 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an unauthenticated user to read commit comments from a private source fork through a public project's merge request discussions due to missing authorization checks.

llama.cpp b2877 before b11935 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability in the ggml-rpc server that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to crash the rpc-server by sending oversized message lengths. After the HELLO handshake, attackers can send a command such as SET_TENSOR with a length above std::vector::max_size(), triggering an uncaught std::length_error that aborts the process and denies service to all clients.

Forge, also called node-forge, is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, publicKey.verify() with the default RSASSA-PKCS1-V1_5 scheme in lib/rsa.js parses the recovered DigestInfo with the lenient BER parser asn1.fromDer() and validates its structure with digestInfoValidator without requiring canonical DER bytes. Non-minimal or indefinite lengths, malformed parameter values, and non-canonical object identifier encodings with padded subidentifiers or trailing bytes can leave attacker-controlled data inside an accepted DigestInfo. When the verifying RSA public key uses a low exponent such as e=3, an attacker can use that encoding slack to forge a signature without the private key. The same path is used by X.509 certificate and PKCS#7 signature verification. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.1.

The Dokan: AI Powered WooCommerce Multivendor Marketplace Solution – Build Your Own Amazon, eBay, Etsy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.3. The vulnerability exists because the `matches_mcp_endpoint()` function applies an unanchored regular expression (`#/(?:woocommerce|dokan)/mcp(?:/|$)#`) against the entire `REQUEST_URI` including the query string, meaning any request that contains the literal substring `/dokan/mcp/` or `/woocommerce/mcp/` anywhere in its URI — including inside a query parameter value — is incorrectly treated as a trusted internal MCP context, causing `scope_product_permissions()` to unconditionally return `true` on WooCommerce's `woocommerce_rest_check_permissions` filter regardless of whether the caller is authenticated. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read full authenticated WooCommerce REST product records for any published product — including private underscore-prefixed meta, purchase notes, downloadable file URLs for paid digital products, catalog-hidden products, and edit-context representations — across the `/wc/v1`, `/wc/v2`, `/wc/v3`, and `/wc-analytics` REST namespaces. The bypass is triggered by appending a query parameter whose value contains the literal string `/dokan/mcp/` to any WooCommerce REST product endpoint (e.g., `/wp-json/wc/v3/products/{id}?x=/dokan/mcp/`); note that percent-encoding the slashes prevents the bypass, as the unencoded literal slash characters are required for the regex to match.

FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, after FreeSWITCH has learned and closed source learning for an RTP peer, read_rtp_packet() and rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c reject RTP from an unrecognized source only after packet classification and, for encrypted calls, SRTP processing. An unauthenticated attacker with UDP reachability to an active RTP or SRTP media port can sustain a foreign-source packet flood that occupies the media read path and prevents legitimate media from entering FreeSWITCH on calls that consume incoming media for relay or echo. The resulting one-way audio allows the affected endpoint to continue hearing the other party, but the other party loses that endpoint's audio, leaving SIP signaling established while the call is unusable for conversation. Transmit-only playback was unaffected in testing. A caller can learn the media port from the SDP answer, while a third party must first discover an active port, and no valid SRTP key is required. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. In 1.11.2 and earlier, rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c uses one session-wide autoadj_tally to learn RTP sources that differ from the address negotiated in SDP. An unauthenticated remote attacker who sends plaintext RTP during call setup can make packets from one or more non-advertised sources reach the threshold before the legitimate endpoint, causing FreeSWITCH to adopt the source of the threshold-crossing packet as the media peer. The attacker can then receive call audio, inject media, and deny media to the legitimate endpoint without being on the media path. FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 adds two opt-in controls, but both default to zero and the release remains affected unless both are configured before RTP session creation. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.11.2.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 15.0.0 until 15.5.29 and 16.4.5, the /_next/image optimizer in self-hosted Next.js deployments can process attacker-supplied SVG content even when dangerouslyAllowSVG is false, which is the default. The SVG reaches a parser that the application intended to keep disabled, increasing exposure to denial of service and vulnerabilities in SVG decoding. This issue is fixed in versions 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. Prior to 15.5.29 and 16.4.5, self-hosted Next.js App Router route handlers and the fetch cache that return a fetched upstream response unchanged can emit a response whose declared framing does not match the body actually sent. When the application is behind an HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy that permits pipelined response queueing, a crafted upstream response can desynchronize responses between clients. The resulting desynchronization can inject a response into another client's queue or disclose another client's response. This issue is fixed in versions 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.2.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications with Cache Components enabled can reuse an outer 'use cache' entry across root param values when a nested 'use cache' call reads a root param through next/root-params and returns a value containing pending promises. React Flight can deliver the ready portion to the outer function before the inner cache finishes publishing its root-param dependencies. The outer entry can then complete and be persisted under a key that omits the root param, causing the first written value to be served for other root param values and allowing the outer entry to ignore nested cache tag invalidation and lifetimes. The leaked value is not attacker controlled and depends on which invocation writes the entry first. This variant does not require an existing inner cache entry or a slow cache handler and is not covered by the fix for CVE-2026-103004. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

The Kirki - Freeform Page Builder, Website Builder & Customizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Unauthorized Data Access in versions up to, and including, 6.4.1 via the `kirki_post_apis` AJAX action's `get-dynamic-content-batch` and `get-collection-batch` endpoints. This is due to the plugin opening these resolvers behind a site-wide, resource-unbound preview token (`EditorPreview::has_valid_token()`) that is NOT bound to the specific page the administrator intended to share, combined with the absence of any `list_users` or `can_user_read_post()` capability check inside `HelperFunctions::get_user_dynamic_content()` and `Collection::get_collection_batch()` — the equivalent checks ARE present on the plugin's own REST route (`FrontendRESTController::get_item_permissions_check()`). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers holding any valid read-only share link to extract from the entire user table every user's `user_email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `nickname`, `registered_date`, arbitrary string-valued `user_meta` (including custom keys such as `billing_phone`), and the e-mail address of every approved commenter — information that WordPress itself withholds from anonymous readers (served only in the `edit` context behind `list_users`).

The User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.14 via the `draft_post()` function. This is due to the function storing the `post_content` parameter via `wp_insert_post()` without the protected-shortcode allow-list check that was introduced in 4.3.14 for the sibling `submit_post()` handler — a gap that `wp_kses` filtering does not close, as it strips only HTML tags while leaving shortcode text such as `[wpuf-registration role="editor"]` intact. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to embed a registration shortcode in a post and cause any site visitor who subsequently registers through the rendered form to receive Editor-level access. The render-time `wpuf_modify_shortcodes` filter that is designed to neutralize protected shortcodes provides no protection here because posts created via the `wpuf_draft_post` AJAX endpoint carry no `_edit_last` post meta, causing the filter to return the content unchanged and allowing the shortcode to render and execute fully.

The Groundhogg plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_title' merge-tag of the [ghr] shortcode in versions up to, and including, 4.10 The post_title replacement is registered with 'nested' => true, so the nested branch of Replacements::do_replacement() returns the merge value through tackle_replacements() without passing it through escape_merge_tags()/escape_shortcodes(); the callback single_post() calls html_entity_decode(get_the_title(), ENT_QUOTES), converting the entity-encoded text that wp_filter_kses leaves intact on a Contributor's post title back into raw HTML, which is then emitted into the rendered post. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.3.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications using the same 'use cache' function directly during rendering and through unstable_cache() can disclose cached data across root params when that function reads a root param. During the first fill after a cold process start, cross-request deduplication allows a concurrent unstable_cache() request to join the direct call's in-flight fill and receive its result before the root param mismatch is rejected. unstable_cache() then persists that result under a key that omits root params, causing later requests for other root param values to receive the same entry until revalidation or eviction. Exploitation requires the unstable_cache() request to arrive while the first fill is in flight. Outside this race, nesting 'use cache' inside unstable_cache() raises an unsupported-operation error, and avoiding that nesting prevents the issue. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 17.0.0, the @libp2p/gossipsub default configuration allows a connected remote peer to submit unsigned subscription RPC metadata for arbitrarily many distinct topic strings. handleReceivedSubscription in packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts creates a persistent topics-map entry for each accepted topic, while allowedTopics is unset by default, decodeRpc maxSubscriptions limits only one RPC rather than aggregate topic bytes, and peer scoring has no subscription-volume penalty. A single peer can therefore grow the topics map and committed heap toward out-of-memory conditions, and disconnecting additionally causes removePeer to scan all accumulated topic entries. This issue is fixed in version 17.0.0.
Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.
Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.
Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

In FRRouting, bgpd frees the same memory twice when dynamic BGP neighbors disconnect, if the peer-group used by a "bgp listen range" also has a Site-of-Origin configured ("neighbor PG soo"). Each dynamic neighbor shares the peer-group's SoO value instead of getting its own copy, but frees it as its own when the neighbor is deleted, which happens as soon as its connection closes. The first disconnect leaves the peer-group pointing at freed memory, and the second disconnect frees it again, causing bgpd to abort and drop all BGP sessions on the router. Any host whose address falls inside the listen range can trigger this by opening and closing two TCP connections to the BGP port, without sending any BGP message and without knowing the AS number, and can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. If the peer-group has a TCP-MD5 password, only hosts that know the password can trigger it. Two ordinary flaps of legitimate dynamic neighbors have the same effect. Between the two frees, displaying the configuration ("show running-config") or establishing a dynamic neighbor also reads the freed memory, which can crash bgpd after a single disconnect. Only configurations that combine a listen range with a SoO on the same peer-group are affected.

Description:


When an HTTP profile and an iRule using the 

MR::message 

route command are configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE)


Impact:










Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.


Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

An improper JWT signature verification vulnerability in CIRCUTOR PowerStudio SCADA WAVE desktop version allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication by submitting an unsigned JWT with the algorithm set to “none”. The shared JWT validation component accepts the token without verifying a cryptographic signature, allowing the attacker to impersonate another user and access protected functionality with that user's privileges.

The FS Poster - WordPress Social media Auto Poster & Scheduler [Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Pinterest] plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery in all versions up to, and including, 8.0.1 via the 'site_url' parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to make web requests to arbitrary locations originating from the web application and can be used to query and modify information from internal services. The Guzzle HTTP client is instantiated with TLS certificate verification disabled and redirect following enabled by default, allowing redirect-based SSRF bypasses and enabling internal port scanning via distinguishable server responses.

A flaw was found in OpenShift Hive. The ClusterClaim controller assigns hive-claim-owner RBAC based on a user-controlled ClusterClaim.spec.namespace and only verifies ClusterPoolRef.ClaimName. A tenant can point a same-named claim at another tenant's ClusterDeployment and obtain get access to that cluster's admin kubeconfig and admin password secrets.

The Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.69 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with shop manager-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The PowerPress Podcasting plugin by Blubrry plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 11.18.2 via the 'podcast-images[] (actually `${feed_slug}-images[]`)' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to read the contents of arbitrary image files on the server, which can contain sensitive information.

The WP Delicious – Recipe Plugin for Food Bloggers (formerly Delicious Recipes) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'details[].icon' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.10.11 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload bypasses wp_kses_post on save because Gutenberg serializes block attribute JSON with JSON_HEX_QUOT, encoding double-quotes as \u0022 so no raw quote or angle bracket appears in post_content; parse_blocks() restores the literal quote at render time, producing the HTML attribute breakout.

The Search Everything plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in versions up to, and including, 8.1.9 via the search_everything AJAX action. The handler registered at `wp_ajax_search_everything` performs no capability check, no ownership check, and no nonce verification before running a WP_Query over `$_GET['s']` and returning the raw WP_Post objects — including the `post_password` field — as JSON. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to extract cleartext passwords for every password-protected post on the site and, when the plugin's draft/attachment/metadata search options are enabled by an administrator, to read draft and pending post contents they otherwise have no capability to view.

The WP Delicious – Recipe Plugin for Food Bloggers (formerly Delicious Recipes) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'recipeTitle' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.10.10 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. WordPress core's block-attribute kses pass strips HTML tags but preserves bare double-quote characters, allowing a payload such as x" onerror="alert(1) to survive both the save pipeline and the render-time strip_tags() call, breaking out of the alt attribute of the rendered img element.

The Meow Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'limit' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.9 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

The AMP for WP – Accelerated Mobile Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.1.19 via comment content rendered on AMP post pages. The plugin registers an output-buffer callback ampforwp_the_content_filter_full() on the 'wp' action (priority 999) that applies a set of tag-agnostic and quote-agnostic regular expressions — notably /onclick=[^>]*/ — to the entire AMP page output after approved comments have already been echoed into it; these regexes do not understand HTML tag or attribute-value boundaries, so a kses-legal comment that places strings like 'onclick="' inside a title attribute value can trigger deletion of the title's closing quote, causing the browser to re-parse what was previously textual content inside the attribute value as live HTML attributes. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page, after an administrator has approved the comment.

Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js. Prior to 2.5.315, an authenticated user with write:pages can store JavaScript expressions in the v-slot:tabs or v-slot:content attributes of page HTML because server/modules/rendering/html-security/renderer.js adds those executable Vue directives to DOMPurify's allowlist. The sanitized output is inserted as rendered page HTML and later compiled by the Vue 2 runtime compiler, so the expressions execute in the Wiki.js origin when another user views the page even when the author lacks write:scripts and administrative permissions. The script runs with the viewer's browser session and can read same-origin data, modify displayed content, present phishing content, or perform actions available to that viewer, including privileged GraphQL operations when a privileged user opens the page. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.315.

Description: 
BIG-IP iControl REST tokens may not expire as expected in all scenarios.   

Impact: 
An attacker who has obtained a token may be able to extend its expiry lifetime unless the token owner deletes it. There is no data plane exposure; this is a control plane issue only.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

The Appointment Booking Plugin – LatePoint | Calendar & Scheduling for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 5.7.7 via the 'key' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract full invoice and receipt records including customer full name, email address, phone number, invoice line items and totals, and the invoice's real access key. This is exploitable via the unauthenticated public routes invoices__view_by_key and transactions__view_receipt_by_key, which apply no ownership, capability, or nonce check before passing the attacker-supplied key into the ORM lookup.

The BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized modification of data due to a misconfigured capability check on the 'update_item_permissions_check' function in all versions up to, and including, 14.4.0. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to enable and disable plugin components.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to require client certificates ("ssl_verify_client on") in a non-default stream virtual server, a remote attacker could bypass verification of client certificates.

Impact:
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass verification of client certificates. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

@fastify/proxy-addr determines which network hops are trusted proxies and backs Fastify's trustProxy setting, so that forwarded headers can be believed. In versions 3.0.0 through 5.1.2, when trustProxy is configured with a zoned IPv6 link-local address, the trust comparison checks only the address bits and ignores the zone identifier, so a host on another link of a multi-homed server that carries the same link-local address is trusted as well. Such an attacker can spoof the X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto headers, making the client IP, host and protocol reported by Fastify attacker-chosen values and defeating IP allowlists, rate limiting and audit logging. Exploitation requires a multi-homed server whose trustProxy is a zoned link-local address and an attacker directly on one of its other links; the default configuration and global, private or loopback trust entries are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/proxy-addr 5.1.3, and users should upgrade to 5.1.3 or later. As a workaround, avoid trusting a zoned link-local address on a multi-homed host and trust a global, private or loopback proxy address instead.

The BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 14.5.0. This is due to missing authorization checks in the `bp_nouveau_ajax_get_single_activity_content` AJAX handler. The function only verifies a nonce that is publicly exposed to any visitor who loads a BuddyPress page, but does not call `bp_activity_user_can_read()` to verify the user has permission to view the activity. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read private group activity content by iterating activity IDs.
Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer.
Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with the square of the message size.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.8 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an unauthenticated user to read restricted job artifact data due to missing authorization checks.

The Soledad theme for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7.7 The public penci_more_post_ajax AJAX action feeds infeedads[ads_code] (base64+urldecoded) to penci_safe_shortcode(), whose allowlist regex inspects only the hyphen-truncated outer shortcode name (e.g. 'adinserter') and never the nested [elementor-element k=.. data=..] tag, so do_shortcode() renders an attacker-chosen Elementor element. The rendered penci-featured-sliders widget passes its unsanitized 'style' setting to include dirname(__FILE__)."/{$style}.php", a path-traversal local file inclusion.

Effect is a TypeScript framework that consists of several packages that work together to help build TypeScript applications. Prior to 3.22.1, Schema.TemplateLiteral schemas containing at least two Schema.String spans compile each span to the ambiguous lazy wildcard [\s\S]*?. Decoding a non-matching untrusted string causes cubic regular expression backtracking, which can block the JavaScript event loop. The issue affects Schema.decodeUnknown, Schema.decodeUnknownSync, Schema.is, and consumers such as HttpApi and @effect/rpc payload decoding. This issue is fixed in version 3.22.1.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260513.0, Draft Workspace identifiers are accepted without verifying that the authenticated user can access the referenced draft. Any authenticated user can enumerate draftWorkspaces, use a disclosed DRAFT_ID with draftWorkspaceEntities to read unpublished reports, descriptions, observables, and other staged intelligence, or place the identifier in the opencti-draft-id header and run mutations that inject entities and relationships into another user's private workspace. The flaw permits cross-user disclosure and tampering but does not cause a denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 7.260513.0.

fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, bin/fzf-tmux validates separately supplied layout sizes but does not validate attached -l and -u layout values before Bash arithmetic expansion, allowing command substitution in a crafted operand to execute as the invoking user during option parsing. The same validation failure lets space-bearing popup geometry options -x, -y, -w, -h, and -p reach an unquoted tmux popup option string and inject additional tmux flags. Exploitation requires less-trusted project configuration, a wrapper, or a plugin to supply the poisoned value and requires the victim to invoke fzf-tmux; normal values are usually trusted, and the script has been superseded by built-in tmux options. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.

fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, trigger-driven zsh completion in shell/completion.zsh uses _fzf_feed_fifo to create a FIFO at the predictable shared path ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fzf-complete-fifo-$$ and continues after removal or creation errors. On a multi-user host, a local attacker can pre-create that path as a symlink so the victim's completion stream overwrites a victim-writable file, potentially enabling code execution when that file is later sourced. A pre-created FIFO can instead disclose a bounded stream of completion candidates or block completion. On default modern hosts, fs.protected_symlinks blocks the overwrite variant, and protected_fifos and protected_regular further limit the FIFO disclosure and blocking variants, so exploitation depends on the relevant kernel protections being disabled and on the victim invoking the affected completion. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.

Converting crafted CP949 input to UTF-8 character encoding and ignoring invalid characters, in the GNU C Library version 2.1 or later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When the CP949 decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\xa2\xe8' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice.  If //IGNORE is set on the destination encoding and this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit this, the target iconv function needs to set //IGNORE on the destination of the conversion and the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input to UTF-8 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.2 through 2.44 may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When the ISO-2022-CN-EXT decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\x0e' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice.  If this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit this, the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

Description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a use-after-free condition in the NGINX worker process, leading to a restart. Exploitation also depends on conditions beyond the attacker’s control. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description:


When BIG-IP APM is provisioned, and a virtual server is configured with an APM access profile and a per-request policy, and the tmm.access.policytrace database key is enabled, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate. The key is disabled by default.












Impact:



Traffic is disrupted
while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system . There
is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.





Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

In nanobot, when sandboxed exec is enabled, the shell executable used to run commands can be selected by the caller and is launched before the sandbox is applied. An attacker who can induce the agent to create an executable in the workspace and select it as the shell can cause that executable to run outside the sandbox (e.g. Linux bubblewrap), with the operating-system permissions of the nanobot process.

This issue affects nanobot (nanobot-ai) from 0.2.1 before 0.4.1.

In nanobot, the WebSocket gateway allows a standard client holding a valid client token to select an existing directory outside the operator-configured workspace as the root of a new conversation. The agent can then read and expose files in that directory that are readable by the nanobot service account.

This issue affects nanobot (nanobot-ai) from 0.3.5 before 0.4.1.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to change the GitLab Duo Code Review consent setting of a parent group due to incorrect authorization checks.

WarehousePG (WHPG) 6.27.1 through 6.27.7 and 7.2.1 through 7.6.1 are affected by an out-of-bounds write vulnerability (CWE-787) in gpfdist, the file server used to load and unload external tables. When gpfdist attaches a request to a session, it sizes two internal arrays from the client-supplied X-GP-SEGMENT-COUNT header and writes to them at the index given by the X-GP-SEGMENT-ID header, without checking that the index is non-negative and smaller than the count (CWE-129). gpfdist does not authenticate callers unless gpfdists is used with client certificate verification, so an attacker who can reach the gpfdist port can crash it with a single HTTP request, failing every external table load or unload that uses that gpfdist instance. gpfdist is normally reachable only from the cluster's internal network.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 16.10 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to configure GitLab Duo settings for groups without an eligible license due to missing authorization checks.

ICRTouch PocketTouch version 1.700 build 2025.3726 contains a default socket password set to the literal value password. Where the default value remains unchanged and is accepted by a TouchPoint POS terminal, an attacker with network access to the terminal’s socket service may authenticate using publicly known credentials.

The order-tracking functionality in ICRTouch ByTable and TouchTakeaway does not adequately verify that a requester is authorized to access the specified order. An unauthenticated remote attacker can modify an order identifier to retrieve information associated with other customers’ orders.

The wallet top-up functionality in ICRTouch ByTable and TouchTakeaway does not adequately protect state-changing requests against CSRF. An attacker-controlled website can cause an authenticated customer’s browser to submit a wallet top-up request and add an attacker-selected charge to the customer’s active cart.

ICRTouch Commander administrative login interface does not adequately restrict repeated authentication attempts. The interface also returns distinguishable responses for multiple authentication states, including different behavior when a `siteID` value is supplied.

ICRTouch Commander administrative interface performs security-sensitive operations through HTTP GET requests and includes an API key in the request query string. GET requests are commonly retained in browser history, proxy logs, server logs, analytics systems, referrer headers, and other intermediary records.

ICRTouch PocketTouch version 1.700 build 2025.3726 transmits the POS socket password in plaintext XML over an unencrypted TCP connection. The protocol does not provide transport-layer encryption to protect credentials from interception.

An attacker able to observe network traffic between a PocketTouch device and a TouchPoint POS terminal can recover the socket password from captured packets.

ICRTouch PocketTouch version 1.700 build 2025.3726 defines hard-coded default values for multiple credential fields, including a socket password and configuration and shutdown passwords. An additional email-related password field is initialized without a value.

The PocketTouch and TouchPoint POS protocol includes a `SAVECONFIG` command that appears capable of overwriting till configuration files remotely. 
An attacker with network access to the POS socket service may be able to submit a crafted `SAVECONFIG` command and replace or modify terminal configuration data.

The PocketTouch and TouchPoint POS `CHECKPAYMENT` workflow accepts a caller-supplied clerk number without adequately verifying that the requesting client is authorized to act as that clerk.
An attacker with access to the POS protocol may be able to specify another employee’s clerk identifier and submit payment-related requests under that identity.

The ICRTouch white-label TouchTakeaway Cordova applications do not implement certificate or public-key pinning for backend HTTPS connections. The applications therefore rely exclusively on the device’s system trust store when validating server certificates.
An attacker who can cause a device to trust an attacker-controlled certificate authority, or who operates through a compromised or improperly issued trusted certificate, may be able to intercept and modify application traffic.

The TouchOffice API `clerkList` endpoint appears to return sensitive clerk authentication data, including clerk PINs and iButton serial numbers. If the endpoint is accessible to callers who do not require access to these values, the API exposes reusable authentication material beyond the minimum information necessary for clerk-list functionality.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.8 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to access GitLab Duo features restricted by group-based access rules due to improper handling of failed updates to those rules.

Multiple Farmasimplex healthcare integration modules do not properly validate TLS certificates, allowing an attacker who can intercept network traffic to impersonate trusted healthcare services and perform man-in-the-middle attacks, potentially leading to disclosure or modification of sensitive data.

The REV.exe module distributed with Farmasimplex contains embedded OAuth client credentials for integration with the IZS platform. An attacker with access to the executable could extract and reuse the credentials, potentially leading to unauthorized access to integration resources or manipulation of associated information, depending on the privileges granted and authentication controls in place.

The CeliachiaRL integration component distributed with Farmasimplex uses shared OAuth credentials across multiple customer installations. An attacker who obtains the credentials from one installation could reuse them against services associated with other installations, potentially leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information or modification of integration data.

An **expression language injection** has been found in the HeaderContentGuard.permit function in publication.py of the content guard in the **Pulpcore** package. The guard is supposed to check a value in a request header. It saves a jq filter and runs that filter against the header when a client asks for content. The filter is not limited to the header, and jq's env builtin also returns the environment of the content process. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can create a header content guard and attach it to a distribution can save a filter that reads that environment. The content request is allowed or denied according to the filter result. Repeating the request lets that attacker or user recover the environment, including Pulp settings held there, such as the Django secret key or the database password.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.4 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user holding an MCP-scoped OAuth token to perform unauthorized issuable state changes on issues and merge requests, including approving and merging, due to incorrect authorization checks.

Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in Apache DataSketches C++. An
  application that deserializes a KLL sketch from an untrusted source
  can have heap memory corrupted by a crafted sketch, because the
  serialized level boundaries were not validated.

  This issue affects Apache DataSketches C++: 2.0.0 through 5.3.0.

  Users are recommended to upgrade to version 5.3.1, which fixes the
  issue.

Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in Apache DataSketches C++. An
  application that deserializes a REQ sketch from an untrusted source
  can have heap memory corrupted by a crafted sketch, because the
  serialized compactor headers were not validated.

The BlockArt Blocks – Gutenberg Blocks, Page Builder Blocks ,WordPress Block Plugin, Sections & Template Library plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.3. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to view the title, excerpt, and full content of other users' draft, pending, and private posts, exposing that content to unauthenticated visitors on the published permalink. This is exploitable by an Author-level user because WordPress's wp_filter_post_kses preserves block-comment JSON in HTML comments, allowing the malicious queryArgs and query[post_status] attributes to survive post saving and execute on every unauthenticated request to the published URL. Exploitation by attackers with contributor-level access and above requires that attacker only needs to see the data themselves (not expose it to unauthenticated visitors) — satisfied by viewing their own preview URL. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, the unauthenticated GET /swagger/doc.json endpoint copies the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host header into the OpenAPI host field without requiring a trusted proxy or validating the value. An attacker can therefore make the served OpenAPI document direct Swagger UI Try it out requests to an attacker-controlled host. When a shared cache or CDN stores and serves that poisoned document to an authenticated user, Swagger UI sends the user's API requests and bearer token to the attacker, enabling disclosure and modification of the user's HomeBox data. Without a shared cache, the attacker can affect only the attacker's own response. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.

HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, a HomeBox password change revokes the user's other session tokens but does not revoke the user's API keys, and API keys have no default API-key expiration. An attacker who has obtained an API key can therefore retain full API-level access after the account owner changes the password and can keep that access indefinitely unless the owner discovers and manually deletes the key by ID. Because the password change terminates other sessions, the surviving API credential can evade the owner's expected containment and detection. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.

The immonex Kickstart plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 1.19.0 via the 'inx-r-cidata (JSON blob containing 'template' and 'template_folders')' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. The filename-level sanitization that strips dot-slash sequences applies only to the template filename component, not to the attacker-supplied template_folders directory paths, rendering it ineffective against directory traversal via that parameter.

OpenAM before 16.1.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows administrators, including delegated realm administrators, to make the server fetch arbitrary URLs through federation configuration wizard metadata URLs. Attackers can enter metadata or OpenID Connect discovery URLs pointing to internal hosts or cloud metadata endpoints to probe the internal network and read partial responses.

OpenAM before 16.1.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows parties registering UMA resource sets to trigger internal requests through unvalidated scope description URLs. Attackers can register resource sets with scope URLs pointing to internal hosts or cloud metadata endpoints, which OpenAM fetches when sending pending-request notification emails, enabling internal network probing.

OpenAM before 16.1.4 does not verify that a signed SAML 1.x assertion or response was signed by the partner named as its issuer, accepting a signature from any certificate in OpenAM's keystore. An attacker holding such a private key, such as a trusted SAML 1.x partner, can forge assertions claiming another partner's issuer and sign in as that partner's users, including privileged ones.

OpenAM from 14.5.1 before 16.1.4 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the OAuth 2.0 device authorization flow that allows attackers to approve device codes when consent is skipped for implied-consent clients. Attackers can start a device authorization and lure a logged-in user to a crafted page, obtaining access and ID tokens to call APIs as that user.

OpenIdentityPlatform OpenAM before 16.1.4 contains an open redirect because WS-Federation logout, SAML v2.0 logout and name-identifier management, SAML v2.0 identity provider finder, and some authentication pages do not check destination URLs against allowed lists. Attackers can craft OpenAM-domain links that send users to arbitrary external sites for phishing.

OpenAM from 14.0.0 before 16.1.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read live session tokens from the notification WebSocket. Attackers can bypass the agent-only check through an unvalidated internal forward on legacy Liberty ID-FF endpoints, collecting iPlanetDirectoryPro tokens to hijack user and administrator sessions.

This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE)



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When BIG-IP APM is provisioned and a per-request policy that includes the Client Information agent and Endpoint Security agents is applied to a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE).

Impact:

Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module module, a specially crafted ClientHello message from an unauthenticated attacker causes forged values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables, affecting virtual server selection. In addition, it may also cause a disagreement with a proxied server terminating the SSL/TLS connection without Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 support.

Impact
This vulnerability may allow an attacker to forge values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables and bypass the NGINX systems stream routing segmentation. As a result, the attacker may be able to route the connection to a privileged or internal backend that should be unreachable and gain access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, the WebSocket reader retains one bytes object for each transport read while reassembling an incomplete frame. A malicious peer can split a frame into many tiny reads so per-object overhead substantially exceeds the payload bytes allowed by max_msg_size. The condition affects a server receiving frames from a malicious client and a client receiving frames from a malicious server, and can cause excessive memory consumption or denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

Grid Community Toolkit before 6.2.20261111 (globus-gss-assist before 12.9) contains a heap out-of-bounds write in globus_gss_assist_token_get_fd() triggered by SSLv2 record lengths below 3. Remote unauthenticated clients can send a crafted GSI handshake record to services like globus-gatekeeper and myproxy to corrupt heap memory and crash the service.

Phison E12 and E18 PCIe SSD controllers contain a Secure Boot bypass vulnerability that allows a privileged local attacker to inject persistent boot-patch tuples into the unsigned, CRC-protected flash ID page read by the BootROM. By overwriting a fuse-derived RAM variable via a crafted patch entry using Phison Vendor Specific Commands, an attacker can force CRC-only firmware verification instead of signature checking, enabling an unsigned firmware image to load and creating a persistent controller-level implant that survives firmware reinstallation and operates below the host operating system.

VB-Audio VB-CABLE before 3.5.2.0 contains out-of-bounds read and write vulnerabilities in the vbaudio_cable64_win10.sys kernel streaming driver's KSPROPSETID_Audio MUTE, VOLUMELEVEL, and PEAKMETER2 property handlers that allow a local standard user to supply an all-channels sentinel value improperly used as a loop terminator or array index instead of being bounds-checked. Attackers can exploit the accessible low-integrity KS filter device object to write attacker-controlled values sequentially into kernel memory, corrupting kernel globals and object pointers, or read past an array boundary to leak kernel memory, resulting in local privilege escalation or denial of service via a kernel bug check.

Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.3.3 and later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash.

When converting from UCS-4, these encoders may encounter a combining base such as U+00E6 and jump ahead by 4 bytes to check the next UCS-4 code point.  The check for end of buffer however does not account for this, which may result in a buffer overread if the following code point has less than 4 bytes remaining.  Exploitation of this bug not only requires attacker control of input and encoding, but also strict control over layout of the input in memory.

@fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads. In versions 7.4.0 through 10.1.8, when the plugin is registered with the attachFieldsToBody option, the saveRequestFiles helper treats any object in the parsed request body that carries truthy file and buffer properties as an uploaded file. An unauthenticated client can forge such an object through a plain JSON request or a JSON-typed multipart field, so attacker-chosen bytes are written to the temporary directory while upload hooks and the file count and size limits are skipped, and the saved entry keeps the attacker's filename verbatim instead of being reduced to its basename. Because that filename can contain parent directory segments, applications that use it as a write destination, as the project README example does, are exposed to an arbitrary relative-path file write from a single request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.9, and users should upgrade to 10.1.9 or later. As a workaround, call saveRequestFiles only after confirming the request is multipart, and reduce each returned filename to its basename or validate it against an allowlist before using it as a destination.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to delete arbitrary patient recall records via the delete_Recall action. Attackers can send POST requests to /interface/main/messages/save.php with a target pid and r_ID to remove recall data without ACL or ownership checks.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the addRecall action of /interface/main/messages/save.php that allows low-privileged authenticated users to modify arbitrary patients' recall data. Attackers can submit a crafted new_pid with recall, contact, provider, facility, and notification preference fields to overwrite records of patients they cannot access.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an arbitrary local file read vulnerability in REST document download, where the controller passes stored uploaded document bytes to Symfony's BinaryFileResponse as a filesystem path instead of returning them as content. Authenticated users with document upload and download access can upload a document containing an absolute pathname, such as the sqlconf.php location, then download it to read server files and recover database credentials.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to read cross-patient FHIR QuestionnaireResponse data by sending the APICSRFTOKEN header.
